label: Game B
nuance_found: Toppings are a real build choice: three different toppings on one tower make a CLUB (+25% to everything), so spreading lettuce, tomato, cheese or bacon beats stacking one, and each tier costs more (45, 80, 120). Towers are not interchangeable: the Cheese Grater shreds armour for knights, the Mustard Squeezer slows, the Pepper Mill clouds. Each stage adds a stage-specific active (flame burners, rinse a lane back, pepper) plus a swat, and aim mode (first / strongest) is switchable. Placing towers late on the path (where my first stage-2 build left the end open and cost me 14 of 20 lives) versus early changed how I played within one stage. Stage 4 punished a thin opening and I lost.
audio: A looping music sample from the first tap, plus sparse sequenced notes; the harness listed no distinct effect sounds in most stretches, so combat and upgrades felt quiet next to the strong visual feedback.
furthest_progress: Cleared stages 1 The Cutting Board (1 star), 2 The Stovetop incl. THE JAR boss (1 star, 6 of 20 bites left) and 3 The Sink (2 stars, 20 of 20 bites); stage 4 Sunday Lunch lost at wave 5 of 12 (lunch eaten, score 3,500), then restarted and was on wave 2 of 12 at 541 s.
control_trouble: Menu buttons moved between the one-row and two-row upgrade panels and I sold a tower by mistake once; otherwise taps were fine. Speed toggle and START overlap near the screen edge on stage 4.
best_moment: Swatting and flaming the Jar boss when it lost its lid and watching combo x43 pile up as the Club towers chewed through it.
worst_moment: Stage 4 flipped from a stress-free stage 3 to losing all 20 bites in about 20 seconds once greasers and a brute got past a thin line.
verdict: This is the better phone game. It is a standard lane-defence template, but the topping and Club rule gives upgrades an actual decision, enemies ask for different towers, each stage hands you a new active ability, and there is a boss with a phase change. It paces itself well: a new stage every minute or two, a combo counter, orders and star ratings. It is not deep like Into the Breach, and the first two stages were far too easy, but by stage 4 I had changed how I placed towers and spent crumbs, which is what I look for. Looks like a finished, juicy toy. I would keep it and come back for three stars.
